title: Enterprise Request Intake: Graduated Networking & Upgrade Triage for Private Deploys
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We need a graded intake and gating process that assigns a deterministic priority and provisioning path for enterprise Private/VPC/on-prem requests that involve networking changes, OS/hypervisor upgrades, or air-gapped constraints. Goal is to reduce ad-hoc decisions, accelerate low-friction requests, and ensure high-risk deployments get preflight engineering and security review.

Context: Current intake is noisy — the same channel surfaces lightweight VPC permission requests and multi-week on-prem upgrade programs. PMs, Solutions, and Eng spend too much time clarifying scope before routing to Dedicated/Private SRE or Solutions Engineering. This ticket defines a graduated triage rubric, a minimal preflight checklist for each risk tier, and a routing matrix that maps to: self-serve templates, Sales-assisted runbooks, Dedicated SRE onboarding, or an Enterprise Integration project.

Scope: Non-bug customer requests (feature/operational intake) only. Focus areas: networking (VPC peering, egress policies, firewall rules, windows air-walls), upgrade tolerance (OS/kernel/hypervisor windows; maintenance cadence), and air-gap/airwall posture (data exfiltration controls, no-internet packaging). Excluded: licensing/contract negotiation, post-deployment incident handling (these are separate playbooks).

Why this matters: Faster, consistent routing will reduce lead time for low-risk customers and free engineering cycles to focus on high-risk integrations. It also reduces scope creep in Solutions engagements and prevents inadvertent SLA exposures when we accept on-prem deployments without contractually defined upgrade windows.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented intake rubric that maps incoming request attributes to Risk Tier (Low/Medium/High) and to a canonical next step (self-serve template, Solutions-assisted, Dedicated SRE, Enterprise Integration). 2) A one-page preflight checklist per risk tier that Solutions/Sales/PS can run in <= 30 minutes for Low/Medium and <= 2 days for High. 3) Integration of the rubric into the intake form (Zendesk/Hub) with fields required for automatic classification. 4) A routing playbook with clear SLAs for response times and who must perform security & network review. 5) Pilot with three enterprise customers and retrospective with metrics (time-to-route, %re-routed, engineering touch-hours).
decisions: Adopt three-tier risk model (Low/Medium/High) rather than binary gate to allow graduated SLA and operational overhead.
Low-tier requests will be handled via self-serve templates + guided checklist; no guaranteed dedicated SRE time.
High-tier requests require security review and a scoped integration statement of work before scheduling maintenance windows.
progress_updates: 2025-02-17: Kickoff with Solutions Eng and Sales to capture common ask patterns; collected 24 anonymized request summaries.
2025-02-21: Drafted initial rubric — scoring factors: network surface area, external egress, upgrade window flexibility, data sensitivity, air-gap requirement.
2025-02-26: Engineering scoping workshop: ENG feedback to add 'kernel/hypervisor version lock' as auto-escalation factor.
2025-03-03: Built first version of the one-page preflight checklists for Low/Medium/High and circulated to Solutions and Security for review.
2025-03-04: Updated intake ticket form prototype and forwarding rules; awaiting Legal & Security sign-off for pilot.
next_steps: Finalize rubric weights and publish as internal Confluence decision doc (owner: Maria).
Add intake fields to Zendesk/Hub + automation rules to tag and route tickets (owner: Ops).
Schedule Security review session for high-tier playbook and define required artefacts (owner: Security team).
Identify three pilot customers (one per industry: fintech, healthcare, retail) and run pilot; capture metrics (owner: Solutions Eng).
patch_notes: 2025-02-17: Created ticket and scoped problem statement. Aisha added initial set of anonymized customer asks.
2025-02-26: Incorporated ENG feedback; added hypervisor version lock as escalation rule.
2025-03-03: Checklist v1 shared with Security; requested clarifications on required logs for air-gapped deployments.
